A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Plan-of-SQLs work. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original Table QA experiments on TabFact, WikiTQ, and FeTaQA, explanation evaluations, and a human study involving 32 participants.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports quantitative accuracy ablations and an error-category analysis.

M1.justification: The atomic natural-language planner, Step-to-SQL conversion, SQL execution, and attribution maps are retained. Both versions already include fallback answering, the FeTaQA adaptation, and one-step planning; v2 Appendix I becomes v3 Appendix J.3. Expanded explanations do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same TabFact, WikiTQ, and FeTaQA tasks and retain the same human-study population. The added ablation and error analyses use existing coverage. Discussions of messy tables and questions requiring external knowledge do not report new evaluations.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same explanation methods and QA baselines, including Text-to-SQL, DATER, CoTable, self-explanation, Binder, LPA, and LLM-only approaches. PAL is newly discussed but is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: v3 adds accuracy evaluation of component ablations and a procedure labeling every incorrect prediction as a planning or fallback error. Existing benchmark splits, backbone models, metrics, and generation settings remain unchanged. The newly supplied verification prompt documents an existing experiment rather than establishing a protocol revision.

E4.justification: v3 Appendix C extends the earlier interpretability ablations and qualitative SQL-removal findings with quantitative QA-accuracy ablations for all three components. Appendix J.2 adds planning-versus-fallback error breakdowns across two datasets and two backbones. These substantially expand the analysis of component importance and failure sources; the illustrative error cases and one-step planning experiment already existed.

E5.justification: The Pearson correlation significance analyses and averaging over four explanation orderings are retained. Neither version reports seed-based uncertainty, confidence intervals, or repeated-run variability, and v3 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Main comparison scores remain unchanged, but v3 adds substantial quantitative results in Tables 11–12: WikiTQ accuracy is 59.32% for full POS versus 27.05% without SQL execution, and planning accounts for 70.7–95.4% of errors across settings. The retained one-step-planning WikiTQ result changes from 54.95% in v2 Table 11 to 59.32% in v3 Table 13, without an explanation establishing why it changed.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and atomicity definition are equivalent. The new discussion invoking SQL's relational completeness supplies informal justification of applicability, rather than a new formal result, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: v3 removes the explicit first-in-the-literature contribution claim, describes abstract-level QA performance as competitive, and narrows the LLM-proxy claim more explicitly to Table QA. The introduction adds a 'within 1–2 points' performance characterization. Interpretability, efficiency, and robustness remain the central contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive discussion of SQL-decomposability boundaries, SQL versus Python, omitting SQL from explanations, and why one-step planning helps. It reinterprets Figure 19's exact-matching failure through planner responsibility and dataset-label inconsistency, and qualifies the WikiTQ table-size interpretation. Existing fallback and FeTaQA limitations are largely relocated, not newly discovered.

D1.justification: v3 adds the prediction-verification judge prompt in Appendix G.1 and points to a different code/data repository. Conversely, it removes v2 Appendix J's Gradio/Flask interface description, study flow, consent text, and participant instructions. Core SQL implementation details and planning prompts remain available.

R1.justification: v3 adds a focused comparison with PAL and references including Cheng et al. (2025), Stoisser et al. (2025), Li et al. (2024), and Wazzan et al. (2025). Some references, including Lipton and Montavon et al., disappear. The overall research positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: Much of the abstract, introduction, methods, findings, discussion, and conclusion is rewritten. SQL execution is merged into the conversion section, baseline descriptions move to Appendix B, self-explanation becomes Appendix A.3, and discussion and limitations are redistributed across the main text and appendices.

P2.justification: The two-column main-paper format changes to a single-column TMLR layout, with extensive changes to table sizing, typography, captions, and figure placement. v3 adds two analysis tables and removes the human-study interface panels. Existing explanation and error-example figures are largely redisplayed rather than new evidence.

improvement.justification: The added accuracy ablations and error breakdown strengthen empirical support, and the verification prompt improves documentation. However, v3 removes detailed human-study materials and introduces an overly broad 'within 1–2 points' claim: unchanged Table 6 shows a 5.10-point GPT-3.5 WikiTQ gap between POS and CoTable. These evidential gains, reproducibility losses, and reporting weaknesses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
